title: Organisation: cell → organism
examples: What is the difference between a tissue and an organ?
Can you give an example of an organ system?
Which is the most complex level of organisation?

explain.say: Today we are learning about how living things are organised.

items: Organ: group of tissues working together
Organ System: group of organs working together

explain.say: A tissue is a group of similar cells working together for a job.
An organ is made up of several different types of tissues working together.
An organ system involves several organs working together to keep the body alive.
The digestive system is an organ system that helps us break down food.
In everyday life, your heart is an organ that works with blood vessels.

faq.q: What is the difference between a tissue and an organ?
faq.a: A tissue is made of one type of cell working together. An organ is made of several different types of tissues working together.
asks: How are tissues different from organs?

faq.q: Does every animal have all four levels of organisation?
faq.a: No, some simpler organisms might not have all these levels. For example, simple plants have different levels.
asks: Is this order always the same?

faq.q: What is the simplest level of organisation?
faq.a: The simplest level we discussed is the cell. All life starts at the cell level.
asks: Is the cell the starting point?

faq.q: Can you give an example of a plant organ system?
faq.a: Plants do not have organ systems like animals do. Instead, they have complex structures like roots and leaves working together.

faq.q: What is the most complex level of organisation?
faq.a: The most complex level we looked at is the organ system, which involves many organs working together.

facts: Cells are the basic, smallest unit of life.
Tissues are groups of similar cells performing a specific job.
Organs combine different tissues to perform a complex function.
Organ systems group organs together for a major life process.

quiz.say: Which level is made of different tissues working together?
quiz.why: An organ requires multiple tissues to perform its specific job, like the stomach.

wrong.0: Cells are the basic unit and do not contain tissues.
wrong.1: A tissue is only one type of cell working together, not multiple types.
wrong.2: An organ system is made of multiple organs, which is a higher level.

quiz.say: If you combine the heart and blood vessels, what level do you form?
quiz.why: The heart and vessels are organs that work together in the circulatory system.

wrong.1: An organ is usually one structure, not a collection of different organs.
wrong.2: Tissues are groups of cells, which is too simple for this combination.
wrong.3: Cells are the smallest unit and cannot be combined this way.

quiz.say: Which structure is correctly ordered from simplest to most complex?
quiz.why: This sequence shows the correct building blocks from smallest to largest.

wrong.0: This order goes from largest to smallest, which is the reverse of building up.
wrong.2: You must start with the cell because it is the fundamental unit of life.
wrong.3: The tissue must come before the organ because the organ is built from tissues.
